subject.title: Browser: support blocked URL paths / domain denylist

question: Should OpenClaw add a public browser navigation deny/warn policy, and what traffic classes should that policy guarantee across top-level navigation, redirects, subframes, subresources, downloads, and browser proxy profiles?
rationale: The request adds a public operator-trusted browser security/config surface, so automation should not choose the permanent denylist or warnlist boundary without maintainer security intent.

options.title: Design Browser Policy Contract First
options.body: Keep this issue open while maintainers define browser-scoped deny/warn semantics and enforcement coverage before implementation.

options.title: Fold Into Broader Egress Policy
options.body: Let the web egress-firewall direction own browser navigation too, but only after it explicitly covers browser-specific behavior.

options.title: Advisory Hints Only
options.body: Avoid an enforceable denylist and only surface best-effort warnings for known bot-blocked sites.

recommendation.title: Design Browser Policy Contract First
recommendation.body: Keep this issue open while maintainers define browser-scoped deny/warn semantics and enforcement coverage before implementation.

likelyOwner.reason: steipete has the strongest current-history signal across browser SSRF config, navigation policy, and shared SSRF helpers.
